title: Consolidate KMS assertion gating and audit-scrub workflow
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: production audits and KMS usage metadata drifted into multiple ad-hoc headers and annotation keys across the ingress path. That made it hard to reliably enforce RBAC v2 resource-scoped grants and to apply consistent data-residency masks in downstream audit storage. This change consolidates the assertion gating surface (the middleware that validates KMS origin, region pin, and consent flags) and centralizes an audit-scrub pipeline that pseudonymizes tenant-sensitive fields while retaining policy traceability. Goals: 1) Provide a single middleware entry that evaluates KMS assertions and emits a canonical assertion bundle for RBAC v2 evaluators; 2) Normalize region-pin and residency hints so routing and KMS selection are deterministic; 3) Implement an audit-scrub stage that pseudonymizes or redacts PII before long-term storage while preserving enough context for compliance investigations; 4) Ship with a migration plan and a shadow rollout to avoid interrupting Dedicated/Private tenants. High-level changes: - new assertion-gate service module (pkg/security/assertion_gate) that canonicalizes KMS headers and evaluates a small policy graph before allowing requests through; - RBAC v2 shim to consume canonical assertion bundles instead of ad-hoc headers; - audit-scrub pipeline (observability/audit/scrub) that tags records with scrub-levels and applies deterministic pseudonyms for tenant identifiers; - new integration tests and linear/metrics hooks (ENG-4120) to validate behavior under network partitions and KMS failovers. Rollout plan: - Stage 1 (shadow): run assertion-gate in shadow mode on inbound traffic for 48 hours and emit diff telemetry. - Stage 2 (opt-in): enable gating for a small percentage (5%) of traffic with a feature flag. - Stage 3 (gradual enforcement): 25% -> 75% -> 100% as metrics show no regressions. Backout is a single feature-flag flip. Checklist: - [x] Canonical header spec documented and added to API contracts - [x] Assertion-gate implementation and unit tests - [x] RBAC shim updated and tested - [x] Audit-scrub stage implemented with configurable scrub-levels - [x] Integration tests for Dedicated/Private pathing - [x] Telemetry: validation success/failure counters and KMS-affinity histograms - [x] Migration plan and runbook added (docs/ops/kms-assertion-rollout.md) Compatibility notes: The canonical assertion bundle is backward-compatible in shadow mode; we provide a short-lived compatibility adapter that translates existing headers to the new bundle for downstream consumers. There is a small token overhead (the bundle adds ~120 bytes) and a CPU cost for pseudonymization at audit ingress; measured median 3rd-percentile CPU spike of 6% under the synthetic ingestion profile used in benchmark-lab. Security/compliance rationale: centralizing gating reduces the surface for misrouted KMS calls and ensures consistent residency checks before RBAC decisions. Pseudonymization in the audit-scrub pipeline addresses long-term storage PII risk while preserving queryability for compliance requests.

changed_files:
Notable files changed (summary):
- pkg/security/assertion_gate/gate.go (new): canonicalizes headers, validates KMS origin, checks region-pin policy.
- pkg/security/assertion_gate/middleware.go (new): injects assertion bundle into request context or emits shadow telemetry.
- pkg/authz/rbacv2/shim.go (mod): accept canonical bundle and translate to internal attributes.
- observability/audit/scrub/scrubber.go (new): scrub-level engine and pseudonymizer.
- tests/integration/kms_assertion_shadow_test.go (new): shadow-mode test harness.
- docs/ops/kms-assertion-rollout.md (new): rollout steps and backout runbook.

release_notes:
- Consolidated KMS assertion gating into a single canonical bundle consumed by RBAC v2; reduces misrouting and improves residency enforcement.
- Central audit-scrub pipeline added; supports configurable pseudonymization and legal-hold passthrough.
- Shadow rollout and SRE runbook included to minimize disruption.
- Minor latency impact at tail under heavy audit-ingest; see ops doc for mitigation steps.
